No conflict — All relevant documents consistently state that the majority of Métis live in urban areas within Canada, particularly in the Prairie provinces.

The evidence from d1, d2, d4, and d5 consistently points to two complementary facts: the majority of Métis live in urban areas [d1, d4, d5] and the majority live within the Prairie provinces (Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba) [d2, d4]. D3 and d6 describe the homeland region, aligning with this geographic focus without contradiction.

The retrieved documents agree on the key claims: most Métis live in cities and their population is concentrated in the Canadian Prairies. Therefore, the final answer can directly combine these consistent facts from the high-credibility sources.

The majority of Métis in Canada live in urban areas [d1, d4, d5]. Geographically, the largest Métis populations are concentrated within the Prairie provinces of Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Manitoba [d2, d4]. Census data indicates about 85% of self-identified Métis live in the five provinces of Alberta, Ontario, Manitoba, British Columbia, and Saskatchewan, with Alberta having the single largest population [d4]. The traditional Métis homeland encompasses this Prairie region along with parts of Ontario, British Columbia, and the Northwest Territories [d1, d3, d6].
